summary: The oldest surviving McDonald's restaurant in the world sits on Florence Avenue in Downey — a 1953 drive-up with golden arches bolted to the building itself, predating the franchise's modern logo — and that oddball claim to fame captures something essential about this city: it's been quietly anchoring southeast Los Angeles County for decades while drawing almost no attention from outsiders. The terrain is dead flat, classic LA Basin floor, with no ridgeline views to speak of but reliable 76°F daytime highs and over nine hours of daily sunshine that make the climate feel perpetually mild. Downey functions as both a bedroom community and a genuine employment node; Kaiser Permanente and Rancho Los Amigos National Rehabilitation Center are major healthcare employers within city limits, and the aerospace legacy runs deep — the Space Shuttle was partially designed in facilities here. At a median household income of $87,400 against a median home price of $728,500, the price-to-income ratio lands around 8.3×, meaning purchasing requires substantial savings or dual incomes, while the $1,892 median rent consumes roughly 26% of gross median income — tight but manageable. Motor vehicle theft stands out at 1,063 per 100K, notably elevated even by LA County standards, a figure worth weighing. Downey is a place with real institutional weight — hospitals, aerospace history, civic infrastructure — wrapped in the unassuming flatness of a city that never learned to advertise itself.
